blocks.x: CLINICAL INDICATION:
[e.g., Anterior knee pain, acute sports trauma, joint effusion, popliteal mass]
SIDE:
[Right / Left / Bilateral]
TECHNIQUE:

High-frequency linear transducer (7.5–15 MHz) gray-scale and power/color Doppler sonography of the anterior, medial, lateral, and posterior compartments of the knee performed in longitudinal and transverse planes with dynamic maneuvers as indicated.
FINDINGS:
ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT:
Suprapatellar Recess / Joint Space: Normal physiological fluid (less than 2–3 mm). No significant joint effusion, hemarthrosis, or synovial hypertrophy.
Quadriceps Tendon: Normal fibrillar echotexture and thickness (6–8 mm) with intact insertion onto the superior patellar pole. No tear or enthesopathy.
Patellar Tendon: Continuous, uniform fibrillar architecture from the inferior patellar pole to the tibial tuberosity (thickness: 3–5 mm). No tendinosis, tear, or calcific deposits.
Prepatellar & Infrapatellar Bursae: Collapsed and unremarkable; no fluid distension or bursitis.
Hoffa's Infrapatellar Fat Pad & Trochlear Cartilage: Normal homogeneous fat pad; smooth, anechoic femoral trochlear articular cartilage (in full flexion).
MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial Collateral Ligament (MCL): Intact superficial and deep fibers from the medial femoral epicondyle to the proximal tibia without thickening or tear.
Pes Anserinus Complex: Normal conjoined tendons; no pes anserine bursitis.
Medial Meniscus (Extruded/Peripheral Aspect): Normal homogeneous triangular echogenicity without peripheral extrusion, tear, or parameniscal cyst.
LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral Collateral Ligament (LCL) & Biceps Femoris Tendon: Intact conjoined insertion onto the fibular head.
Iliotibial (IT) Band: Normal fibrillar appearance over the lateral femoral condyle without underlying fluid distension.
Lateral Meniscus (Peripheral Aspect): Intact peripheral margin without extrusion or parameniscal cyst.
POSTERIOR COMPARTMENT (POPLITEAL FOSSA):
Baker's Cyst (Semimembranosus-Gastrocnemius Bursa): Absent; no fluid neck extending between the medial head of the gastrocnemius and semimembranosus tendons.
Popliteal Neurovascular Bundle: Popliteal artery and vein are patent with normal compressibility and Doppler flow; tibial and common peroneal nerves are normal in caliber.

[Primary conclusion / Normal knee ultrasound statement]

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Mild anterior knee discomfort; rule out effusion or tendinopathy.

subs.title: Findings
items: High-frequency sonographic evaluation of the anterior, medial, lateral, and posterior compartments of the right knee demonstrates intact, normal fibrillar architecture of the quadriceps and patellar tendons without thickening, tendinosis, or tear.
The suprapatellar recess contains only a trace physiological film of fluid without effusion or synovial thickening.
The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and the iliotibial band are intact.
The peripheral margins of the medial and lateral menisci are unremarkable without parameniscal cysts.
No Baker's cyst or popliteal mass is identified, and the popliteal vessels are patent.

subs.title: Impression
items: Normal right knee ultrasound. No evidence of joint effusion, tendon or ligament tear, or popliteal cyst.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Acute inability to extend the left knee and palpable suprapatellar gap following a fall on a flexed knee.

subs.title: Findings
items: There is complete, full-thickness discontinuity of the distal left quadriceps tendon approximately 1.2 cm proximal to the superior pole of the patella, with a 2.4 cm retraction gap filled by a heterogeneous, hypoechoic hematoma.
The patella is inferiorly displaced (patella baja) with redundancy and buckling of the patellar tendon.
A large, complex suprapatellar joint effusion containing layering echogenic fluid-fluid levels (lipohemarthrosis) is present.

subs.title: Impression
items: Complete full-thickness tear of the distal left quadriceps tendon with a 2.4 cm retraction gap and associated hematoma.
Large suprapatellar lipohemarthrosis, suspicious for an occult intra-articular fracture. Urgent orthopedic surgical consultation recommended.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Valgus stress injury to the right knee during soccer; medial joint line pain.

subs.title: Findings
items: Grade II Partial Tear: The right medial collateral ligament (MCL) is diffusely thickened (measuring 7.5 mm) and hypoechoic with focal partial disruption of the deep meniscofemoral fibers and surrounding periligamentous edema/fluid, though superficial fibers remain continuous on gentle valgus stress.

Grade III Complete Tear Alternative: [Or: Complete full-thickness disruption of both superficial and deep MCL fibers at the femoral attachment with wavy, retracted tendon ends and widening of the medial joint space during dynamic valgus stress.]
A small anechoic suprapatellar effusion is noted.

subs.title: Impression
items: High-grade partial (Grade II) tear of the right medial collateral ligament with surrounding periligamentous edema.
Small reactive knee joint effusion.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Acute tense knee swelling and severe pain immediately after blunt trauma; initial radiographs inconclusive.

subs.title: Findings
items: Markedly distending the suprapatellar recess is a large, complex joint effusion (measuring 2.8 cm in AP thickness) demonstrating three distinct horizontal fluid-fluid layers on supine scanning: a superficial echogenic fat layer floating anteriorly, a middle hypoechoic serum layer, and a dependent echogenic cellular/blood layer ("lipohemarthrosis"), which shifts briskly with transducer compression.
The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

subs.title: Impression
items: Large suprapatellar lipohemarthrosis, pathognomonic for an occult intra-articular fracture (such as a tibial plateau or patellar fracture).
CT scan of the knee is recommended for definitive fracture characterization and surgical planning.

bank.title: 5. Jumper's Knee (Patellar Tendinopathy) & Osgood-Schlatter Disease (Non-Traumatic / Overuse)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Chronic inferior patellar pain in a basketball player (or tibial tuberosity pain in an adolescent).

subs.title: Findings
items: Patellar Tendinopathy: The proximal left patellar tendon is fusiformly thickened (measuring 8.2 mm AP) at its attachment to the inferior pole of the patella, demonstrating focal ill-defined hypoechogenicity, loss of normal fibrillar architecture, and marked intratendinous neovascularity on power Doppler.

[If Adolescent / Osgood-Schlatter]: Fragmentation and irregularity of the ossification center of the tibial tuberosity is noted, accompanied by distal patellar tendon thickening, surrounding soft tissue swelling, and distension of the deep infrapatellar bursa.

subs.title: Impression
items: Severe proximal left patellar tendinopathy ("Jumper's knee") with active hyperemia on power Doppler; no full-thickness tear.

bank.title: 6. Baker's Cyst (Popliteal Cyst) & Ruptured Baker's Cyst (Non-Traumatic)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Posterior knee fullness and sudden-onset calf pain/swelling mimicking deep vein thrombosis (DVT).

subs.title: Findings
items: Intact Baker's Cyst: Within the posteromedial popliteal fossa, there is a well-defined, thin-walled anechoic cystic collection measuring 4.8 x 2.1 x 3.2 cm demonstrating a classic "crescent/speech-bubble" neck extending between the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus tendon.

[If Ruptured]: The inferior pole of the cyst demonstrates a pointed, irregular beak-like configuration with surrounding ill-defined hypoechoic fluid dissecting caudally along the fascial planes of the medial gastrocnemius muscle and subcutaneous tissue. The popliteal and posterior tibial veins are completely compressible with normal Doppler flow, excluding DVT.

subs.title: Impression
items: Ruptured left Baker's cyst (popliteal cyst) with fluid dissecting into the medial calf fascial planes.
Negative lower extremity venous Doppler; no evidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT).

bank.title: 7. Inflammatory Synovitis / Joint Effusion & Prepatellar Bursitis (Non-Traumatic)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Chronic knee swelling, morning stiffness, and anterior focal fluctuant mass.

subs.title: Findings
items: Suprapatellar Recess: Marked distension of the suprapatellar recess containing moderate anechoic fluid alongside lobulated, hypoechoic, frond-like synovial hypertrophy (measuring up to 6 mm) that is non-compressible and demonstrates Grade 2 intra-synovial hyperemia on power Doppler, consistent with active proliferative synovitis.

Prepatellar Bursa: Anterior to the patella, the prepatellar bursa is distended by a well-circumscribed, thick-walled hypoechoic fluid collection measuring 3.5 x 1.2 cm with mild peripheral hyperemia ("housemaid's knee").

subs.title: Impression
items: Moderate knee joint effusion with active proliferative synovitis on power Doppler.
Prepatellar bursitis. Correlate with rheumatologic/infectious workup as clinically indicated.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Focal, firm, tender lump along the lateral joint line.

subs.title: Findings
items: Along the lateral joint line, immediately adjacent to the peripheral margin of the lateral meniscus, there is a well-defined, lobulated, multiseptated anechoic/hypoechoic cyst measuring 1.6 x 1.1 cm with posterior acoustic enhancement and no internal Doppler flow.
The adjacent lateral meniscus is extruded beyond the tibial plateau margin by 4.5 mm and contains a linear hypoechoic cleft extending to its peripheral border.

subs.title: Impression
items: Lateral parameniscal cyst (1.6 cm) associated with lateral meniscal extrusion and suspected underlying horizontal meniscal tear.
MRI of the knee is recommended for complete intra-articular meniscal and cartilage evaluation.
